question: Which party won the Jalandhar (a city in Punjab) Lok Sabha bypoll election held in May 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Aam Aadmi Party.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• AAP was formed in November **2012**, led by Arvind Kejriwal, after the India Against Corruption movement, to fight for clean governance and transparency.
 
• The Aam Aadmi Party** (AAP)** gained the status of a national party on **April 10, 2023**. 
 
• The most recent government formation by the **Aam Aadmi Party **(AAP) took place in Punjab after the **2022 Assembly elections**.
 
• A National Party is a political party recognized in four or more states or one that has won at least **11** seats in the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• It was founded in **1885**, INC played a crucial role in India's independence movement and is one of the oldest political parties in India.
 
• Its key figures include Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Indira Gandhi, who shaped Indian politics and policy.
 
• Although it has faced significant challenges in recent elections, INC remains influential in Indian politics, holding a significant number of seats in various state assemblies and the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**
 
 
• It was founded in **1980**, The BJP is rooted in Hindutva ideology and represents right-wing politics in India.
 
• Under Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, the BJP has implemented significant policies like GST and the Make in India initiative, leading to substantial electoral success.
 
 
 
• **Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)**
 
 
• **​**It was founded in **1920**, SAD advocates for the rights and interests of the Sikh community in Punjab.
 
• The party has formed the government in Punjab multiple times and holds significant influence in state politics.
